To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we performed whole exome analysis of a sporadic bAVMs patient and we detected several novel variants affecting genes potentially involved in vascular differentiation, including a de novo variant in the STK4 gene.

(a) we identified 11 novel likely gene-disruptive variants and 9 rare known variants affecting genes involved in vascular differentiation; (b) we analyzed these variants in molecular networks at Cystoscope platform, suggesting their involvement in bAVMs pathogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of sporadic bAVMs.
the identification of novel likely gene-disruptive variants, inherited or de novo, and with their possible involvement in sporadic bAVMs pathogenesis.
the detection of novel likely gene-disruptive variants in sporadic cases of brain arteriovenovascular malformation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic background of bAVM pathophysiology is still elusive and that further investigations should be carried out to elucidate the genetic basis of this disease.
our study is a first attempt to identify novel genes and variants associated with sporadic bAVMs, and that the results are promising and deserve to be further investigated.

, even if we are not able to demonstrate a direct link between these genetic variants and the development of bAVM, we can suggest that the variants here detected are good candidates for further studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high-throughput sequencing is a powerful tool to identify novel likely gene-disruptive variants in sporadic bAVMs.

the study of genetic basis of sporadic bAVMs could lead to the identification of novel genes involved in vascular development and, in turn, to the development of novel therapeutic strategies for this condition.

the use of high-throughput sequencing technologies in sporadic cases of bAVM is a promising tool to detect novel genetic variations, which could be involved in the pathogenesis of this vascular lesion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of next generation sequencing is a powerful approach in order to detect rare and novel variants that could be involved in the pathogenesis of bavm lesions.
the use of next generation sequencing in a sporadic case of bAVM allows us to discover new candidate variants and genes involved in bAVM development.
next generation sequencing is an effective tool for the detection of rare variants and it is a pivotal step for the identification of new genes involved in bAVM development.
